profile.headline: Senior System Software Engineer at NVIDIA
profile.summary:
- Experience in software design and development of network security systems
- Experience in Linux kernel and embedded system development    
- Experience in Mobile Application development (iOS, Android, Windows Phone)
- Solid knowledge of computer network architecture, switching, routhing and TCP/IP stack

positions.title: Sr. Software Engineer - Vehicle
positions.description:
-Integrating embedded software for customer programs with a primary focus on OTA updates, delivering in-vehicle prototypes and hands-on technical support to OEMs.
- Integrated SNMP functionality onto NXP NETC switch by porting from lightweight IP stack.
- Developed core networking and security software for the vehicle gateway, implementing dynamic firewalling, policy-based routing, and multi-APN management using the embedded Linux stack (iptables/Netfilter) to ensure secure V2C connectivity.
positions.insights: Skills: Over-the-Air update · SNMP · SOME/IP · Linux Firewalls · Iptables · NAT · VLAN · C++ · AUTOSAR

positions.title: Software Engineer - Core Network
positions.description: Developing the Networking Knowledge Plane - Making link quality, usage, and attribution information available to system components

positions.title: Staff Embedded Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Enhanced SLBC IPsec VPN load-balancing to support more customer-requested features: Dead Peer Detection (DPD), IKE/IPsec SA auto-negotiation, Auto-Discovery VPN (ADVPN), HA, ESP sequence number sync
- Enhanced IPsec VPN load-balancing to chassis-based firewall FortiGate-7000 series
- Enhanced IPsec VPN load-balancing to other networking components: dynamic routing (BGP, RIP, and OSPF), SD-WAN, local ingress/egress traffic, Link Monitor, NPU VDOM link

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer, Android Systems
positions.description:
MobileIron develops mobile application management (MAM) software. I work in the MAM-Android group, developing application wrapping middleware for Android applications.

Application wrapping consists of modifying, or "wrapping", an existing app so that the app conforms to specific security policies set by the MAM administrator. Examples of such policies are:

• Is user authentication required?
• May the app store data on the device?
• May the app access enterprise data stored in the cloud?
• If so, should the app encrypt the enterprise data that it reads/writes?
• May the app use specific APIs, such as copy/paste or file sharing?

[Technologies used: Linux Internal, Android Security, Java/C++, Reverse Engineering,  ARM Assembly]
